data.one_liner: Detects when your widget appears or disappears from the screen.
data.what_it_does: FocusDetector provides callbacks to get notified every time a widget appears or disappears from the screen. It behaves similarly to onResume/onPause on Android or viewDidAppear/viewDidDisappear on iOS. It can trigger events when navigating, scrolling the widget in or out of view, or turning the device screen on and off.
use_when: You need to turn on and off resource-consuming features like camera, location, or bluetooth based on widget visibility.
You need to sync data with a remote API or local database when a screen gains focus.
You need to pause and resume video or audio playback when navigating away from a screen.
avoid_when: You only need basic page route transitions without sub-widget visibility detection.
strengths: Handles both visibility changes and app foreground/background transitions.
weaknesses: Relies on visibility_detector under the hood, which inherits its performance characteristics.
